stem.text: For a particular reversible reaction the backward reaction is endothermic.
The activation energy of the backward reaction is $160\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
It can be assumed that the backward reaction proceeds by a mechanism that is the exact reverse of the mechanism for the forward reaction.
Which statement about the activation energy of the forward reaction is correct?

A.text: The activation energy of the forward reaction is equal to $-160\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

B.text: The activation energy of the forward reaction is $0\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ but less than $+160\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

C.text: The activation energy of the forward reaction is equal to $+160\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

D.text: The activation energy of the forward reaction is greater than $+160\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
